purpose: Ceritinib is used to treat a specific type of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has a gene change called ALK-positive. It is used when the cancer has spread to other parts of the body. Your doctor will test your tumor to make sure this medicine is right for you.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have an abnormal protein called ALK that tells them to grow out of control. Ceritinib works like a 'lock blocker' — it attaches to that abnormal protein and turns it off, slowing or stopping cancer cell growth. Because it targets a specific change in the cancer cells, it works differently from traditional chemotherapy.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, stomach pain, and feeling tired. You may also notice decreased appetite, constipation, or changes in your blood sugar or liver enzymes. Most of these can be managed, so let your care team know if they bother you.
warnings: Ceritinib can cause serious lung problems, liver damage, heart rhythm changes (QT prolongation), vision problems, and high blood sugar. Tell your doctor right away if you have trouble breathing, yellowing of skin or eyes, fast or irregular heartbeat, or severe stomach pain. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they can increase the medication's effects.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 450 mg (three 150 mg capsules) taken by mouth once a day WITH food, at the same time each day. Taking it with food helps reduce stomach side effects. Swallow the capsules whole — do not crush or chew them. If you miss a dose, skip it and take the next one as scheduled; do not double up.
